newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN WIN TITLE DESPITE SEASON OF SCANDALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN WIN TITLE DESPITE SEASON OF SCANDALS.

text.p: Bayern Munich ended a championship campaign of squabbling and scandals by clinching a record 14th German league title on Saturday.

First-half headed goals from Christian Ziege and Mehmet Scholl and second-half strikes from Italian striker Ruggiero Rizzitelli and forward Marcel Witeczek secured the Bavarians a 4-2 victory over VfB Stuttgart on the penultimate day of the season.
The victory gave Bayern an unassailable four-point lead over Bayer Leverkusen whose hopes vanished in a crushing 4-0 defeat at Cologne.
Bayern have won the Bundesliga 13 times since German league football began in 1963. Their other championship came in 1932 when the title was decided after a final.
But Germany's richest club has had to cast aside an array of scandals throughout the season to clinch its first title since 1994.

Germany captain Juergen Klinsmann, who has been embroiled in a public row with club captain Lothar Matthaeus, is leaving Bayern to join Italy's Sampdoria after next week's final game because he is fed up with the atmosphere at a club.
Chairman Franz Beckenbauer has often been very critical of a team of highly-paid internationals who have had to hold crisis meetings when results have not gone their way.

Nevertheless Klinsmann, who has never won the Bundesliga before, and wing-back Christian Ziege, who is set to join AC Milan, both left Munich's Olympic stadium pitch holding back the tears on Saturday after their last games for Bayern at the ground.
The problems of a controversial season were all forgotten in the celebrations.
"I am happy for both of them. It's a great way for them to go," business manager Uli Hoeness said. "We didn't expect it to go our way completely with us winning and Leverkusen losing.
Ziege added: "This has shown that we have been able to pull ourselves together (at the right time)."
Stuttgart took the early initiative in a tense local derby, played in front of a capacity 63,000 crowd, when they went ahead with a 17th-minute goal from midfielder Danny Schwarz.
But three minutes later Ziege equalised with a header from close range.
VfB's hopes of stopping Bayern winning the title suffered a major setback in the 23rd minute when their Bulgarian international Krasimir Balakov was sent off for complaining to the referee.

Another header from close range from Scholl on the stroke of halftime gave the Bavarians a 2-1 lead at the break. With news coming from Cologne that Leverkusen were 2-0 down at halftime, Bayern knew that the title was there for the taking.
German international Fredi Bobic equalised for Stuttgart with a header in the 51st minute. But in the 65th minute, Rizzitelli put Bayern ahead again.
In the 78th minute Witeczek struck a brilliant shot from 25 metres out to seal the win and set off wild celebrations.
Leverkusen's place in next year's European Cup is a major achievement for a club who just avoided relegation last season.
"We're disappointed but we've had a great season," said the club's sports director and former international Rudi Voeller. "We had to push forward today and you take risks doing that."
Bayern's Italian coach Giovanni Trapattoni added: "We've needed some luck during the season but that's normal. I never thought Leverkusen would lose today."
